capabilities.name: conversation.read
capabilities.lets: Read bots' conversations and follow them live; sealed card fields never reach it

capabilities.name: conversation.post
capabilities.lets: Add a note to a conversation, or send a bot a message; a turn it starts is the plugin's, never the user's
capabilities.ok: adds notes and sends messages to bots

capabilities.name: memory.read
capabilities.lets: Read bots' memories

capabilities.name: bots.read
capabilities.lets: Read the list of bots and their settings
capabilities.ok: sees your bots and their settings

capabilities.name: routines.read
capabilities.lets: Read the list of routines and their runs
capabilities.ok: sees your routines and their runs

capabilities.name: computers.read
capabilities.lets: Read the computer registry: each computer's folders, level and state
capabilities.ok: sees your computers, their folders and levels

capabilities.name: computers.control
capabilities.lets: Take and release holds and the user-working mark, learn where Clover's windows are, and say when an action is running
capabilities.ok: controls the screen and input of your computers

capabilities.name: devices.read
capabilities.lets: Read the user's devices: their names, kinds, links, which one is the main, and which are online

capabilities.name: approvals
capabilities.lets: Hear which cards are pending, never their text, and place their sealed frames

capabilities.name: files
capabilities.lets: Read and write files through the folder tree, inside the fence
capabilities.ok: reads and writes files on your computers

capabilities.name: project.write
capabilities.lets: Let its hooks and stdio MCP servers change files in the session's project folders (never `.git/hooks`, `.git/config` or a credential file); without it, those folders are read-only to them
capabilities.ok: changes files in your project folders

capabilities.name: browser
capabilities.lets: Drive the Clover Browser through its API

capabilities.name: terminal
capabilities.lets: Show the user's terminals on their computers, fed only with what the runtime derives from the user's own key presses and pastes; never on a computer at read-only

capabilities.name: plugins.install
capabilities.lets: Install plugins from the indexes and npm for the user to OK: each lands found, with its sealed OK card, and nothing it installs runs before that OK
capabilities.ok: installs plugins for you to OK

capabilities.name: usage.read
capabilities.lets: Read usage rows and plan readings
capabilities.ok: sees your usage and plan readings

capabilities.name: logs.read
capabilities.lets: Read Clover's logs and every plugin's

capabilities.name: notify
capabilities.lets: Send the user a notification through the notifiers

capabilities.name: audio
capabilities.lets: Record and play audio through the app; it records only while push-to-talk is held, unless the user turns listening on

capabilities.name: call:<plugin-id>
capabilities.lets: Run that plugin's commands

capabilities.name: network:public
capabilities.lets: Reach any public host through the core's fetch, with its web floors: public addresses only, the dangerous-domain list, a card before a private address, and the audit log; its components reach no host from it
capabilities.ok: connects to any public website, through Clover's web safeguards

capabilities.name: network:<host>
capabilities.lets: Reach that host through the core's fetch, which adds the plugin's own keys and tokens, and from the plugin's components, which reach no other host

corePoints.name: bot
corePoints.doc: Builds `<bot-instructions>`, picks the default model, keys memory by the bot's id (§6).

corePoints.name: models
corePoints.runsOn: every computer running a session; started when first needed
corePoints.doc: Calls the adapter, or the declared endpoint, for every turn; the welcome guide reads the sign-in methods (§3.3).
corePoints.shipsWith: every provider today's agent SDK has

corePoints.name: mcpServers
corePoints.runsOn: local servers on each computer they are installed on; remote servers on the computer running the session (§9.1)
corePoints.doc: Dispatches tool calls, builds the MCP block and shows MCP Apps pages.

corePoints.name: skills
corePoints.doc: Indexes them in `Glossary` (§6.8).

corePoints.name: agents
corePoints.doc: Offers these presets to `Agent`: backend, model, effort, instructions, computer, root folder, plugins (§9.3).

corePoints.name: agentBackends
corePoints.runsOn: the computer the agent is placed on
corePoints.doc: Starts agents for `Agent`: an ACP agent or a vendor cloud agent (§9.3).
corePoints.shipsWith: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Gemini CLI, DeepSeek, Winter's coding agent

corePoints.name: hooks
corePoints.runsOn: every computer running a session; started when first needed
corePoints.doc: Calls them in the turn loop; a hook can block or adjust, never replace the runtime or skip approvals.

corePoints.name: commands
corePoints.doc: Runs a plugin's public functions for any client at once, with no model turn (§5.4).

corePoints.name: triggers
corePoints.doc: Arms them for routine files (§7).

corePoints.name: voices
corePoints.runsOn: the computer the user is talking on
corePoints.doc: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech for the bot's voice choice (§6.6).

corePoints.name: computerProviders
corePoints.doc: Creates, resizes and deletes the VMs that cloud computer folders describe (§9.2).

corePoints.name: computer
corePoints.doc: A cloud computer, created after the user's OK (§9.2).

corePoints.name: relays
corePoints.doc: Carries encrypted traffic when two devices can't connect directly, or holds encrypted sync mail (§8.3).
corePoints.shipsWith: n0's public relays; the cloud computer relay

corePoints.name: notifiers
corePoints.doc: Wakes companions when something happens (§10).

corePoints.name: companions
corePoints.doc: Serves a remote client within the fixed list of remote calls (§10).

corePoints.name: themes
corePoints.doc: Applies the base theme, the user's global theme and each bot's theme in its tab (§5.5).

corePoints.name: app.root
corePoints.doc: Mounts the main window's root: the shell (§5.5).

corePoints.name: app.surface
corePoints.doc: Opens top-level floating windows.

corePoints.name: bot.tab
corePoints.doc: Holds each bot's tab, which the shell shows.

corePoints.name: locales
corePoints.doc: Supplies strings for the core's own text and each plugin's keys, in the user's language (§5.5).

dataPoints.name: webhook.ingress
dataPoints.doc: Ways for webhooks to reach a device: the waifucave forwarder, the user's cloud computer, a tunnel (§7).

handler.description: An export of `host.entry`: a function, or for a service (a `webhook.ingress` entry, a notifier) an object of functions, whose caller names the one it calls.

dataPoints.name: avatar.packs
dataPoints.doc: Avatar files with their format and portrait, so an avatar pack is a data plugin (§5.5).

file.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

portrait.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: app.root
spots.doc: The main window's root: the shell, which declares every other spot.

spots.name: app.surface
spots.doc: Top-level floating windows, such as the island and the Dispatch pill; `window` says how they float.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: bot.tab
spots.doc: Each bot's tab, keyed by bot; an entry with no key fills every bot without one of its own, except in a bot's own plugin, where a keyless entry takes that bot's id as its key.

spots.name: sidebar
spots.doc: The sidebar.

spots.name: sidebar.bot
spots.doc: A bot's row in the sidebar, keyed by bot: its state and what waits for the user.

spots.name: sidebar.app
spots.doc: App buttons in the sidebar; `opens` names the `main` and `panel` key it shows.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: main
spots.doc: The main area, keyed by route: bot, agent, settings, plugins, app.

spots.name: panel
spots.doc: The panel host, keyed by panel: each panel (session, terminal, diff, files, browser) is a plugin of its own, and replaceable. A panel for some sessions only says so with `when.session` (the code-only panels: `"coding"`); a key no plugin fills shows the host's placeholder.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: panel.view
spots.doc: A spot inside each panel view, keyed by the view's id.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: settings.section
spots.doc: A section of the settings screen, which the settings part (`main` key `settings`) declares.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: status
spots.doc: The shell's status bar; the inherited `tile` becomes an entry here (§12).

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: bot.header
spots.doc: The tab's header.

spots.name: bot.header.action
spots.doc: Buttons in the tab's header.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: bot.stage
spots.doc: The stage, where the avatar stands.

spots.name: bot.side
spots.doc: The tab's side area.

spots.name: conversation
spots.doc: The conversation view.

spots.name: composer
spots.doc: The composer; a send counts as the user's only on a real key press or click (§5.5). Its entry also gets the host callbacks (`useComposerHost`): the models its session can switch to, a model switch, interrupt and stop; each acting one needs the user's own key press or click, and a model switch on a bot's main conversation is a sealed card unless it is the default composer's.

spots.name: avatar
spots.doc: Draws the bot's avatar, keyed by the avatar file's format (`vrm`, `live2d`, or a plugin's own; `AVATAR_FORMATS`), and lip-syncs it from `speech` (a `SpeechFeed`).

spots.name: composer.action
spots.doc: The composer's buttons, keyed by action id.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: conversation.message
spots.doc: One message, keyed by kind; the `approval` cell can't be hidden. The `tool` cell gets a run of calls.

spots.name: conversation.message.extra
spots.doc: Add-ons under each message.

spots.name: tool.result
spots.doc: A tool's result, keyed by tool name (`mcp__blender__*`); `item` is the one call.

spots.name: menu.message
spots.doc: Items in a message's menu. Picking one runs its `command` (`command.run`) with these props as its args; the message's text is there only for a plugin with `conversation.read`.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: file.preview
spots.doc: A file's preview wherever one shows, keyed by media type (`image/*`); in a bot's plugin, only inside its tab.

spots.name: island.tab
spots.doc: A tab of the island, such as Needs you, Devices or Usage. The island labels a third-party tab with its plugin's name, and only the `clover` tree's tabs raise the strip's attention.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

spots.name: pill.target
spots.doc: Something the Dispatch pill can message besides the bots: `handler` (a `PillTargetHandler`) gets the user's words. The pill names it with its plugin's name, and leaves out one titled as a bot.

icon.description: A path relative to the plugin folder, with `/`; it must resolve inside it.

handler.description: An export of `host.entry`: a function, or for a service (a `webhook.ingress` entry, a notifier) an object of functions, whose caller names the one it calls.

tokens.name: color.canvas
tokens.doc: The base plane: the sidebar and the app's background.

tokens.name: color.surface
tokens.doc: The content plane: the conversation and settings pages.

tokens.name: color.raised
tokens.doc: One step above the content: tool output, inner cards, code blocks.

tokens.name: color.control
tokens.doc: Small controls: chips, toggle tracks, icon circles.

tokens.name: color.float
tokens.doc: Anything floating above content: menus, popovers, palettes.

tokens.name: color.hairline
tokens.doc: Dividers and rims on the canvas and the content plane.

tokens.name: color.hairline.raised
tokens.doc: The same rule drawn on raised and control surfaces.

tokens.name: color.hover
tokens.doc: A row's fill under the pointer.

tokens.name: color.selected
tokens.doc: A selected row's fill. Navigation stays neutral: never the accent.

tokens.name: sidebar.tint
tokens.doc: The sidebar over the window's material.

tokens.name: sidebar.solid
tokens.doc: The sidebar where the window has no material (Linux).

tokens.name: titlebar.tint
tokens.doc: The title bar over what scrolls under it.

tokens.name: titlebar.height
tokens.doc: The title bar's height, its rule included.

tokens.name: color.text.muted
tokens.doc: Quiet meta: timestamps, labels, trailing words.

tokens.name: color.accent
tokens.doc: The accent as the OS gives it: focus, marks, a checkbox, small controls. Filled controls take `color.accent.fill`.

tokens.name: color.accent.fill
tokens.doc: Filled controls: primary actions, the send button, a toggle's on state. The accent darkened in its own hue until white text reads at 4.5:1.

tokens.name: color.accent.text
tokens.doc: The accent carrying text, at 4.5:1 or more on the content plane.

tokens.name: color.accent.soft
tokens.doc: A wash of the accent: a chosen chip, a highlighted mention.

tokens.name: color.accent.contrast
tokens.doc: Labels and glyphs on `color.accent.fill`, at 4.5:1 or more (`auto` resolves it: white on the darkened fill).

tokens.name: color.accent.glyph
tokens.doc: Glyphs on the raw `color.accent` (✓, a dot), at 3:1 or more (`auto` resolves it).

tokens.name: color.accent.ink
tokens.doc: The theme's dark ink for glyphs on an accent, where white falls short of 3:1.

tokens.name: color.attention
tokens.doc: Needs you: a waiting card, a question for the user.

tokens.name: color.danger
tokens.doc: Errors and actions that destroy something.

tokens.name: color.diff.added.soft
tokens.doc: The tint behind a line a diff adds.

tokens.name: color.diff.removed.soft
tokens.doc: The tint behind a line a diff removes.

tokens.name: color.unread
tokens.doc: The unread dot: a neutral grey.

tokens.name: color.brand
tokens.doc: Clover's mark: the one place the brand pink shows, since the accent follows the OS.

tokens.name: bubble.bot.background
tokens.doc: The bot's message. Clear by default: replies sit on the content plane.

tokens.name: card.muted
tokens.doc: The card's meta: the computer, the tool.

tokens.name: card.approve.text
tokens.doc: The approve button's label and glyph (`auto` resolves it at 4.5:1).

tokens.name: card.button.radius
tokens.doc: The approve and deny buttons' corner.

tokens.name: card.font.family
tokens.default: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", "Noto Sans", Ubuntu, Cantarell, sans-serif

tokens.name: font.sans
tokens.default: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", "Noto Sans", Ubuntu, Cantarell, sans-serif
tokens.doc: The interface and body face: each OS's own.

tokens.name: font.serif
tokens.default: ui-serif, "New York", "Iowan Old Style", "Noto Serif", Georgia, serif

tokens.name: font.mono
tokens.default: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Mono", "JetBrains Mono", "DejaVu Sans Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace

tokens.name: font.display
tokens.default: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", "Noto Sans", Ubuntu, Cantarell, sans-serif
tokens.doc: Bot names, greetings and the wordmark.

tokens.name: font.size.code
tokens.doc: Code, commands and paths in running text.

tokens.name: font.line.tight
tokens.doc: Line height for one-line labels and headings.

tokens.name: font.line.code
tokens.doc: Line height for code and tool output.

tokens.name: radius.huge
tokens.doc: The largest corners: sheets, the stage.

tokens.name: shadow.float
tokens.doc: Something floating: a menu, a popover.

tokens.name: motion.spring.response
tokens.doc: The surfaces' spring: seconds per oscillation.

tokens.name: island.rim
tokens.doc: A floating island card's hairline rim.

tokens.name: island.faint
tokens.doc: The island's faintest words: positions, hints.

tokens.name: island.attention
tokens.doc: Waiting for you: the hand and its count.

tokens.name: island.success
tokens.doc: A status that is well: running, connected.

tokens.name: island.danger
tokens.doc: A status that is not: an error, a force quit.

tokens.name: island.option.hover
tokens.doc: An option row's fill under the pointer.

tokens.name: island.card
tokens.doc: An inner card inside the open island: a Needs-you request.

tokens.name: pill.text
tokens.doc: What the user types into the pill.

tokens.name: pill.attention
tokens.doc: A card's kind glyph; a child that needs you.

tokens.name: pill.accept
tokens.doc: The ✓ circle on a pill card.

tokens.name: pill.accept.text
tokens.doc: The ✓ glyph on a pill card.

tokens.name: pill.option
tokens.doc: A question option's fill on a pill card.

tokens.name: pill.option.hover
tokens.doc: A question option's fill under the pointer.

tokens.name: pill.plume.tail
tokens.doc: The working plume where it cools.

tokens.name: pill.plume.hot
tokens.doc: The working plume at the nozzle.

tokens.name: stage.floor
tokens.doc: The soft pool of shadow under the avatar.

tokens.name: stage.text
tokens.doc: Credits and notes on the stage.
